:::{#exm-entropy-coin}
#### Entropy of a coin flip

Let $X$ be the result of one flip of a coin
with $\P(X=1) = \prob$ and $\P(X=0) = 1 - \prob$
([Bernoulli distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-bernoulli)).
By @thm-entropy-discrete, using logarithms to base 2,

$$H(X) = -\prob \log_2 \prob - (1 - \prob) \log_2 (1 - \prob).$$

For a fair coin, $\prob = 1/2$, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
H(X)
&= -\tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{2} \\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{1}{2} \\
&= 1 \text{ bit}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For a coin that always lands heads, $\prob = 1$, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
H(X) &= -1 \cdot \log_2 1 - 0 \\
&= 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

The outcome is known in advance, so there is no uncertainty to measure.
An entropy of $0$ means that all of the probability is on one outcome.

:::
